solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like sis, off ill in medical procedure

indicators.note: ill here means badly, in a poor state, so the letters before it are put into a sickly new order

explanation.surface: A sister who is like her sibling, both off work sick, during some treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' looks like part of the story of a sick sister but tells you to rearrange LIKE SIS OFF; 'in' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiss of life is mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, an emergency first-aid technique.

clue.text: Celebrated skater upset occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every third letter of the two words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A famous skater had a bad fall now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks the 2nd, 5th, 8th and 11th letters of SKATER UPSET. 'Celebrated skater' wants to be a famous name like Torvill; the definition is only 'Celebrated'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a festival or anniversary is to observe or celebrate it, as in keeping Christmas.

clue.text: Rushed out thus, attempted to turn first pair

parts.note: thus means so, in that way

indicators.note: the first pair of letters of the word for attempted swap round, read the other way

parts.note: attempted means tried

explanation.surface: Someone dashed out, having tried to flip the leading couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn first pair' swaps the opening two letters of TRIED, giving RTIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sortie is to make a sudden attack or rush out from a defended position.

clue.text: Novel with troops succeeds among faint-hearts

indicators.note: succeeds means comes after, so the with-troops part follows the among-faint-hearts part

parts.note: among can mean of, as in one of the crowd
mice are timid people, faint-hearts
with means and, alongside
troops are men, soldiers

explanation.surface: A book in which soldiers triumph among the cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like 'triumphs' but means 'comes after'; 'among' giving OF is the sense of one of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Of Mice and Men is John Steinbeck's 1937 novella about two itinerant ranch workers.

clue.text: Notice my upset in fortune produces one feeling superior

indicators.note: in puts the notice and the upturned word inside the word for fortune

parts.note: fortune means luck
a notice is an advertisement, AD

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word my reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: Seeing an advertisement upset me so much that my luck made someone smug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns a word upside down, so 'my' reads YM; 'in' sets the notice and YM inside the word for fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Muck is British slang for a woman who behaves as though she is grander than everyone else.

clue.text: Club's striker trying Shearer's headers and angles

parts.note: the face of a golf club is the part that strikes the ball

indicators.note: headers here means the first letters, the heads of the two words

explanation.surface: A football club's forward attempting Alan Shearer's headed goals and angled shots.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a famous English centre-forward, so 'striker' and 'headers' look like football; they are a golf club's FACE and the first letters T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Facets are aspects or sides of a question, much as angles are ways of looking at it.

clue.text: Outlook that is embodied by car manufacturer

indicators.note: embodied by means contained in the body of, so the abbreviation goes inside the car maker

parts.note: VW is Volkswagen, the German car maker
that is translates the Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A car company's outlook, as expressed in its products.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook and a view are both a way of seeing things or a scene in front of you.

clue.text: Jimmy discovered Irish duck

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover removed, so the first and last letters of Jimmy go

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: A man called Jimmy found an Irish duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means uncovered: JIMMY loses J and Y to give IMM. 'duck' is the verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to plunge them under water, which is what immerse means.

clue.text: Guard's trick that may keep hunter in place

definitions.text: that may keep hunter in place

parts.note: a guard is a watch, and the 's adds an S
a trap is a trick to catch someone out

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's ruse to keep a huntsman where he is.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter here is a pocket watch with a hinged cover over its face, not a person who hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap holds a timepiece such as a hunter on the wrist.

clue.text: Doctors, say, attending fight involving the same leader of aliens knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so everything built so far is read in reverse
involving means taking in, so the fight goes round the same-plus-leader letters

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
idem is Latin for the same

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word aliens

explanation.surface: Medics on duty at a punch-up where the aliens' chief got floored again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' builds SCIDEMARAP, which 'knocked back' reverses. The definition leans on the prefix para-, beside: those who attend alongside doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedics work alongside doctors, the Greek prefix para meaning beside, and attend medical emergencies.

clue.text: Blue material produced by corporations from the East

indicators.note: from the East in an across clue means read from right to left

parts.note: a corporation is jocular slang for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Pornography made by Asian companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporations' looks like companies but is the old joke sense of a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in British usage means indecent, and smut is obscene writing or pictures.

clue.text: Confounding logical men, he becomes Renaissance figure

indicators.note: confounding means mixing up and confusing, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: By baffling rational men, he turns into a hero of the Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo was the Italian sculptor and painter of the Sistine Chapel, central to the High Renaissance.

clue.text: Metal zither inspired new composer's intros

indicators.note: intros are introductions, the opening letters of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A zither's metallic sound inspired a new composer's introductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic element, used to galvanise iron.

clue.text: Regular advance covers most of audition for old leading lady

indicators.note: covers means goes round, so the march surrounds the shortened trial

parts.note: a march is a steady advance in regular steps

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter of the word for audition

parts.note: an audition is a trial for a performer

explanation.surface: An old actress, once the star, sails through most of an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter; 'covers' wraps the march around what is left, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is an elderly woman who heads a family, its leading lady.

clue.text: Solvers go astray with blond, getting new ideas

parts.note: the setter addresses the solvers as you

indicators.note: astray means off course, so the letters of go and blond wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Solvers went off track with a fair-haired person and got fresh thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Young blood means fresh, youthful vigour and the new ideas newcomers bring.

clue.text: Soldiers caper about new artillery

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: about means around, so the dance goes round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: to caper is to skip about, to dance

explanation.surface: Troops frolic around fresh big guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military weaponry, especially heavy guns and ammunition.

clue.text: Warning from Mad Hatter

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of the word it describes are scrambled

explanation.surface: A caution issued by the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a warning of harm to come, as in the threat of rain.

clue.text: Disliked concealing dry bananas with added water

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the word for disliked goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: disliked means hated

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of dry are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone who hated dried bananas has them rehydrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is the anagram signal (crazy), giving YDR, and 'concealing' hides that inside the word for disliked, right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrated describes something that has had water absorbed or combined into it.

clue.text: Definitely not nuts, initially supporting Wanderers

parts.note: a definite refusal is no
nuts means mad, crazy

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word supporting

explanation.surface: Not at all crazy, at first, about backing Wolverhampton Wanderers football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanderers is the nickname of several English football clubs, which 'supporting' plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are people with no fixed home who travel from place to place.

clue.text: Noble king penetrates resistance

indicators.note: penetrates means gets inside, so the letter for king goes into the resistance movement

parts.note: the Maquis was the French Resistance in the Second World War
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An aristocratic monarch breaks through opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking above an earl or count and below a duke.

clue.text: Daisy confused over law — it can make cash from case?

definitions.text: it can make cash from case?

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the rearranged name is spread over and around the word for law
confused means mixed up, so the letters of Daisy are rearranged

parts.note: lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: Daisy is baffled by the law; perhaps the case could make money?
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the name into DYSIA, which 'over' spreads around the Latin for law. The definition is a playful example: one letter mistaken turns 'case' into 'cash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a reading difficulty in which letters may be confused, such as reading one word as another.

clue.text: Vote in favour of adopting decree produces that certain something

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the word for in favour of takes in the decree

parts.note: in favour of means for
an act is a decree or law

explanation.surface: Backing a ruling with your vote yields star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The X factor is an indefinable special quality that makes someone stand out, also a TV talent show.

clue.text: Bill has very cool opinion

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement, AD
to ice is to cool something

explanation.surface: A man called Bill holds a very cool view.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance given as someone's recommendation or view.

clue.text: Plastic Bertrand takes on European drinks provider

indicators.note: takes on means takes in, so the remoulded name absorbs the letter for European
plastic means pliable and reshapable, so the letters of Bertrand are moulded anew

explanation.surface: The Belgian singer Plastic Bertrand takes on a European who serves drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastic Bertrand was a Belgian punk singer, famous for Ça Plane Pour Moi; 'Plastic' is the anagram signal. BERTRAND rearranged gives BARTENDR, which takes in E.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks at a bar, so supplies them to customers.

clue.text: Deft Jayawardene attacks covers

indicators.note: covers means holds inside, so the two words conceal the answer within them

explanation.surface: A skilful Sri Lankan batsman goes after the fielders in the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahela Jayawardene is a Sri Lankan cricketer, and the covers are a fielding position on the off side, so 'covers' looks like cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can mean skilful and adroit, as in a neat piece of work.

clue.text: Scraps bad bits in brandy?

definitions.meaning: ..., as in ... and ends, are scraps and leftovers
the first, third and fifth letters of brandy, its odd-numbered letters, spell bad

explanation.surface: Throws out the nasty fragments floating in a cognac.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: B, A, D are the odd-numbered letters of BRANDY, and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are odd-numbered positions and also leftover scraps, as in odds and sods.

clue.text: Fidelio's finale, fluid composition

indicators.note: finale means the end, so the last letter of Fidelio is taken

parts.note: pus is a fluid formed in infected tissue

explanation.surface: The finale of Beethoven's opera Fidelio is a flowing work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical work, numbered in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Obscure study admitting note is badly handled

parts.note: to mist something is to blur or obscure it

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for study takes the note inside

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An unclear study lets in a note that is being treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistreated means abused or treated cruelly, mishandled.

clue.text: Dim zero's about to go for seconds

indicators.note: to go for means to be swapped out in favour of, so one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A stupid nobody's about to go back for more helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zero's' is zero has; 'Dim' is the adjective for gloomy light, not stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk as an adjective, now poetic, means shadowy, darkish, like the light at twilight.

clue.text: Parts of bed are in front of tables

parts.note: to head something is to be at its front, in front of it
boards are tables, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Bits of a bed come before tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Headboards are the upright panels at the top end of a bed frame.
